candidates.title: Preassemble an ER32 collet into its eccentric clamping nut
candidates.objective: Orient a compatible ER32 collet and nut, engage the collet groove with the marked eccentric ring, and perform the prescribed tilt-and-roll motion until the collet snaps into retention, without threading the nut onto a holder.
candidates.success_conditions: After both grippers release, the collet remains correctly retained for 3 seconds and survives a calibrated light withdrawal check. Zero score for axial forcing, inverted assembly, false or scripted retention, permanent deformation, damage, dropped parts, or state overwrite. Correct orientation and initial groove capture may receive partial credit but do not constitute success.
candidates.industrial_value: REGO-FIX defines collet-to-nut preassembly as part of the ER tooling procedure and warns that improper assembly can damage collet concentricity or destroy the nut.
candidates.dexterity: High: an eccentric lip must first capture a narrow groove, followed by changing-axis insertion and elastic snap engagement rather than ordinary peg insertion.

evidence.locator: ER System Operating Manual, page 1, “Assembling collet and clamping nut”

candidates.asset_plan: Acquire a compatible physical ER32 collet/nut pair or manufacturer-authorized internal CAD, then measure the groove, lip, eccentricity, lead-in, deflection, and engagement forces. Validate correct-entry retention, wrong-angle rejection, removal resistance, damage thresholds, and reset repeatability before any YAM demonstration. Reject the task if pinned Isaac Sim 6.1 rigid contact cannot reproduce the essential compliant snap without a validated compliant model.
candidates.risk: The essential internal retention geometry and elastic behavior are absent from the acquired material. A nominal ER32 envelope or scripted latch would not be an acceptable substitute.
missing_evidence: Manufacturer-authorized internal eccentric-ring geometry or measurements from a compatible physical pair
Evidence that the required elastic engagement is reproducible in the pinned runtime without artificial latching

candidates.title: Align AZ-100 end-of-arm tooling to the mold centerline and lock the adjustment
candidates.objective: On a de-energized representative AZ-100 vertical-adjustment fixture, loosen the adjusting-screw jam nut and two clamp bolts, rotate the adjusting screw to align the tooling datum with the mold centerline, tighten both clamps, and retighten the jam nut without shifting alignment.
candidates.success_conditions: After tool release and a 3-second hold, the tooling datum remains within a hardware-derived centerline tolerance and every fastener is within its measured service window. Zero score for unsafe energization, shortcut motion of unrelated clamps, incorrect order, loose locks, stripped threads, guide damage, dropped tools, or state overwrite. Partial credit distinguishes safe unlocking, correct adjustment, pre-lock alignment, and retained post-lock alignment.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer’s maintenance procedure explicitly uses the adjustment to place end-of-arm tooling at the mold centerline, making it a robot setup operation affecting the tooling-to-process interface.
candidates.dexterity: High: the robot must coordinate three locking elements with fine screw adjustment and resist tightening reactions that can disturb the calibrated state.

evidence.locator: AZ-100 Series Robot Installation and Maintenance Manual, page 24, section 4.1.1, step 2

candidates.asset_plan: Obtain reference-hardware measurements for screw pitch, travel, clamp geometry, tool access, fastener sizes, and service torques. Model the screw and arm with rigid revolute/prismatic constraints so displacement results from physical screw rotation. Validate unlock dependence, direction, pitch, clamp retention, jam-nut reaction, overload behavior, and repeatable reset before YAM integration.
candidates.risk: The procedure is established, but the acquired manual does not provide the dimensions, pitch, torque limits, or permissible centerline error needed for defensible physics and scoring.
missing_evidence: Fastener sizes and service torque windows

candidates.title: Register and secure a robot proximity switch beneath its actuator
candidates.objective: Using an independently authored full-scale fixture grounded in the AZ-100 procedure, retract the rigid cylinder, partially loosen the switch-mount screws, slide the proximity switch beneath its actuator until it registers, tighten it without losing registration, and repeat at the extended endpoint.
candidates.success_conditions: At both retracted and extended endpoints, robot-applied motions alone place the actuator past the switch centerline, maintain a sensing gap of at most 6 mm, trigger the indicator solely through physical relative pose, and leave the switch secured for 3 seconds after release. Zero score for powered adjustment, skipping initial retraction, moving the actuator mount as a shortcut, registering only one endpoint, actuator collision, loose or stripped screws, dropped tools, scripted sensor success, teleportation, or state overwrite. Partial credit is awarded for safe initialization, correct screw release, one geometrically valid endpoint, and registration retained after tightening.
candidates.industrial_value: The AZ-100 maintenance manual requires proximity-switch adjustment after position changes and specifies registration at both cylinder endpoints. The task therefore represents recurring calibration of an industrial robot’s motion-limit sensing rather than generic switch operation.
candidates.dexterity: Moderate-to-high: it combines partial fastener release, constrained sliding, feedback-guided registration, sub-centimeter clearance control, holding against tightening reaction, and repetition across two articulated states.

evidence.locator: AZ-100 Series Robot Installation and Maintenance Manual, page 30, section 4.2.1, step 3
AZ-100 Series Robot Installation and Maintenance Manual, page 30, section 4.2.1, note

candidates.asset_plan: Build a clearly labeled representative, not exact-product, rigid fixture with a slotted switch bracket, retained mount screws, rigid actuator, and two cylinder endpoints matching the documented arrangement. Use the documented 6 mm boundary and over-center requirement. Choose and record testable modeling assumptions for screw size, slot length, tightening window, cylinder stroke, and sensor hysteresis; calibrate them on the fixture before scoring. Implement the indicator only as a function of actuator-to-sensor geometry. First validate screw retention, sliding only while loosened, the 6 mm boundary, over-center registration, collision rejection, tightening drift, reset repeatability, fingertip clearance, and YAM reach in Isaac Sim 6.1.0 at YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730.
candidates.risk: The fixture will not claim to reproduce exact proprietary AZ-100 dimensions. Remaining unspecified dimensions are nonessential, explicitly testable fixture parameters; the sourced retention mechanism—screws clamping a sliding switch mount—and sensing relationship are sufficient. A synchronized novelty review must still be repeated before submission because cached records are not authoritative live state.

selection_reason: This is the only ready candidate: the official procedure establishes the slide-under-actuator mechanism, two-endpoint workflow, and quantitative 6 mm sensing constraint, while a representative rigid fixture can preserve those essential mechanics without claiming an exact product replica. It offers meaningful calibration, alignment, fastening, force-control, and bimanual demands within the pinned YAM runtime. The ER32 task depends on unverified compliant retention geometry, and the centerline-adjustment task lacks essential pitch, torque, and tolerance data.
